decision: The documented actual outcomes and successful methods support pausing the reviewed incremental entropy r5 options and considering the already frozen pulse-block-displacement-r1 as a bounded replacement after rotating-reservoir, thermoelastic-rod and hydrodynamic-heating priority. This is a research-allocation judgment, not a proof that the entropy family cannot be hardened.

scope.actual_reads: Frozen assessment/audit/review, r3/r4 apparatus and successful final functions, selected emitted public commands, failure readout functions, existing causal diagnostic, nearest archive author/source/outcome evidence, and frozen pulse assessment/prior peer.
scope.not_claimed: No new numerical, model, Docker, Git or literature run. This is not a complete second causal audit of every old native command or an empirical test of a new r5 or pulse task.

entropy-anomaly__RdJNzcW.finding: The saved 2D implementation inverts the full rank-three Kronecker-sum relaxation operator for anisotropic drag plus Lorentz coupling. Public probes repair a tensor contraction and check the anisotropic zero-field limit; the final result is a physical pass.

entropy-anomaly__JBmKZft.finding: The saved implementation independently assembles the eight-dimensional velocity tensor operator, contracts its inverse with drag, and tests signed magnetic fields. It solves the matrix-drag physics, rather than fitting an isotropic coefficient.

entropy-anomaly__kAwt6WT.finding: Public commands and final code retain temperature curvature, the first-order tilted operator, a periodic Poisson correction, its gradient coupling and the fast cubic-velocity covariance. The mean-only calibration was not treated as evidence that positional variance was complete.

entropy-anomaly__roBD9hX.finding: The saved reduced-period implementation includes the same fast/slow tilted reduction with physical-coordinate derivatives. Its exploratory Fourier scaling mismatch is repaired before submission; the final result is a physical pass.

failure_qualification.r3_dc8qEkC: Retains the zero-field final coefficient, but public polynomial kinetic-repair attempts already targeted the correct physical issue and produced wrong coefficients. Preserve mixed_failure; this is not a clean physical failure that could support a 0/3 qualification.
failure_qualification.r4_xksyJtc: Fit/interface-only update retains positional occupation variance. The existing fixed-friction diagnostic adds the fast entropy variance and reduces all hidden errors from roughly .986-.991 to roughly 1e-5. Its diagnostic and source hashes match; no rerun was made.
failure_qualification.successful_r4_equivalence: Existing off-grid diagnostic differences for the two successful tilted implementations are 8.44e-15 and 5.33e-15. This corroborates their final physics, despite resolved exploratory algebra/scaling errors.

generality_limits: The r3 code is explicitly two-dimensional and the r4 code evaluates a one-dimensional sinusoidal profile with a specified fast coefficient. They are not already implementations of arbitrary dimension, arbitrary reservoirs or every cumulant.

Nevertheless, the actual matrix inversion and tilted/Poisson structure represent the relevant physical contributions. Changing coefficients, Fourier content, dimensions or cumulant order alone would reuse these mechanisms and add derivation or numerical work without a demonstrated new physical bottleneck.

Combining anisotropic magnetic relaxation with entropy variance could require substantial new algebra. This record supplies no independently validated new apparatus/calibration/readout showing that such a combination tests a distinct missed constraint. Its difficulty remains unmeasured.
The small trial counts do not estimate universal solver success. No outcome is pooled across revisions or replaced by historical favorable screens.

alternatives_reviewed.evidence: Chemical-route-power actual source combines route currents before entropy evaluation; oracle resolves each route. Its three trials corrected that distinction. Magnetic-bath-transfer also has three thermostat-readout passes.
alternatives_reviewed.assessment: A bath-label adaptation alone repeats solved physical attribution.

alternatives_reviewed.evidence: Thermal r11 three passes reconstruct local-bath covariance; active-bath-work three passes retain fast force-velocity correlations. Current rotating r2 explicitly changes contact location and connector strain work.
alternatives_reviewed.assessment: The proposed entropy variants overlap those solved or already prioritized mechanisms; no separate validated r5 remains.

alternatives_reviewed.evidence: Thermal r12 three passes include stored energy and both endpoint/current correlations. Entropy r4 explicitly qualifies that kinetic endpoints may alter the full exponential-moment domain even though they do not change its requested first two rates.
alternatives_reviewed.assessment: Finite-window variance alone repeats r12. A tail-domain observable may be genuinely different, but no ordinary finite readout, shared identifiable calibration, stable margin or independent practical reference is established here. Keep it an open research possibility.

replacement.basis: Whole-body mechanical displacement versus canonical wave momentum is distinct from the reviewed thermal entropy mechanisms; optical transit is already correct in both controls. Existing peer records its reference-independence limits.
replacement.qualification: Scientifically frozen and unmeasured. Scientific/local source-control separation is not evidence of Luna difficulty or qualification. Preserve every eventual outcome; no launch or archival action is authorized by this peer itself.
